list.name: runner
list.label: Runner (regex)
list.description: Filters the deadchannel Runners, Recent Beats, and Haunt Log panels by username regex. Empty matches everyone.

panels.title: Top INFO Messages
panels.description: Most frequent INFO messages - spot noisy logs worth silencing.

targets.expr: {service.name=~"$service"} severity:INFO | stats by ("service.name", _msg) count() info_logs_total | sort by (info_logs_total desc) | limit 8

panels.title: Top WARN Messages
panels.description: Most frequent WARN messages - early warning signal before things escalate.

targets.expr: {service.name=~"$service"} severity:WARN | stats by ("service.name", _msg) count() warn_logs_total | sort by (warn_logs_total desc) | limit 8

panels.title: Top Error Messages
panels.description: Highest-count raw ERROR messages in the selected time range. Useful for seeing repeated noise before filtering it.

targets.expr: {service.name=~"$service"} severity:ERROR | stats by ("service.name", _msg) count() error_logs_total | sort by (error_logs_total desc) | limit 8

panels.title: Log Volume by Severity
panels.description: Log count stacked by severity - red ERROR bursts are visible at a glance.

panels.title: Service Logs
panels.description: Selected service logs for first-pass investigation.

panels.title: Error Logs: late-web
panels.description: Severity ERROR logs for late-web.

panels.title: Error Logs: late-ssh
panels.description: Severity ERROR logs for late-ssh.

panels.title: Service Call Edges
panels.description: Request rate between services from the OTel servicegraph connector. Shows who calls whom.

panels.title: Top Slowest Routes (p99)
panels.description: Slowest HTTP routes by p99 latency across all services

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, service_name, http_request_method, http_route) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_name=~"$service", http_route!=""}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Recent Traces: late-web
panels.description: Latest late-web traces from VictoriaTraces.

panels.title: Recent Traces: late-ssh
panels.description: Latest late-ssh traces from VictoriaTraces.

panels.title: Recent Error Traces: late-web
panels.description: Recent late-web traces with error spans from VictoriaTraces.

panels.title: Recent Error Traces: late-ssh
panels.description: Recent late-ssh traces with error spans from VictoriaTraces.

panels.title: SSH Sessions
panels.description: Current active SSH sessions

panels.title: SSH Traffic
panels.description: SSH connections and successful client pairings

panels.title: Interaction Rate
panels.description: Chat sends, votes, and page views

panels.title: Reliability Signals
panels.description: Frame drops and late-web now-playing fetch results

panels.title: CLI Pair Starts
panels.description: Pair session starts by SSH mode and client platform

panels.title: CLI Pair Active
panels.description: Current active pair sessions by SSH mode and client platform

panels.title: Daily Puzzle Wins by Mode
panels.description: Boards solved on a session over the range, daily and personal apart. Counted where the board ends, so personal boards (never a GameWon) show here too.

panels.title: Daily Puzzle Wins by Difficulty
panels.description: Solved boards by difficulty, both modes. Le Word and Rubik's Cube have one board a day and are left out.

panels.title: Share Rate per Daily Win (%)
panels.description: Share cards copied per fresh daily win. The number that says which daily people brag about.

panels.title: Win Rate, Losable Dailies (%)

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (game, mode, difficulty) (increase(late_ssh_arcade_finishes_total{finish="won",game=~"le_word|minesweeper"}[$__range])) / sum by (game, mode, difficulty) (increase(late_ssh_arcade_finishes_total{game=~"le_word|minesweeper"}[$__range]))

panels.description: Won over finished boards for the two dailies that can be lost (Le Word out of guesses, Minesweeper out of lives).

panels.title: Active Time by Screen
panels.description: Session time on each screen with a key pressed in the last five minutes. Idle terminals left open are counted apart (presence=idle).

panels.title: Active Time by Arcade Game
panels.description: Active session time with an Arcade board open, by game (dailies and score runs).

panels.title: Sessions per Screen (active)
panels.description: Seconds of active attention per second: the average number of active sessions looking at each screen.

panels.title: Door, Table & Match Wins
panels.description: Wins outside the Arcade dailies. Lateania is left out: its GameWon fires per mob kill (family=lateania), which would drown the rest.

panels.title: Render Rate
panels.description: Frames drawn (by trigger) vs clean world ticks that skipped the draw entirely (the dirty gate)

panels.title: Clean Skip Ratio (%)
panels.description: Share of render passes the dirty gate skipped; higher = more idle sessions settling clean

panels.title: Draws per Session
panels.description: Average frames drawn per second per active session (pre-adaptive baseline was ~15; mostly-idle fleet should sit well under 2)

panels.title: Render Stalls
panels.description: Output-budget guard: paused render passes and forced disconnects for clients not reading their stream

panels.title: First Contact Ladder
panels.description: Beats delivered per stage over the selected range. Counters are per-pod and reset on restart, so this sums each pod's high-water mark instead of the live value: a deploy never zeroes the ladder.

panels.title: Gate Verdicts
panels.description: Connects by eligibility verdict, the same reset-safe sum. One count per connect, not per person: which leg turns people away, and how often.

panels.title: Bio Screens
panels.description: AI bio-screen outcomes. Claimed once per bio text per day, so a flapping API costs at most one call per person per day.

panels.title: Beats Over Time
panels.description: When the ladder actually fires. Bars are beats per interval by stage; the slow burn should show as scattered singles, never a cluster.

panels.title: Runners
panels.description: One row per person on the ladder, read off the deadchannel log lines: the highest glitch, name, and whisper hit seen, when the invitation went out and when they joined, how many sessions armed, when they were last seen, and the latest gate verdict with its three legs (hours need 8, settings keys need 2, bio needs 100 chars before a screen is spent). Logs keep 7 days, so a rung reached earlier than that shows as an empty cell: users.settings stays the source of truth. Filter with the Runner variable or the column filters.

targets.expr: _msg:"first contact" OR _msg:"deadchannel joined" | filter username:* | filter username:~"$runner" | stats by (username) max(hits) if (_msg:"clock glitch burst") glitch, max(hits) if (_msg:"name flicker hit") name, max(hits) if (_msg:"whisper delivered") whisper, max(_time) if (_msg:"invitation sent") invited_at, max(_time) if (_msg:"deadchannel joined") joined_at, count() if (_msg:"first contact armed") sessions, max(_time) last_seen, row_max(_time, verdict, active_hours, touched_settings, bio_chars, bio) if (_msg:"gate evaluated") last_gate | unpack_json from last_gate fields (verdict, active_hours, touched_settings, bio_chars, bio) | delete last_gate | sort by (last_seen desc)

panels.title: Recent Beats
panels.description: What just happened on the ladder, newest first: hits (forced ones say so), whispers, invitations, joins, runner births, bio screens, and /haunt flag flips. Arming and gate lines are left out; they live in the Runners table and the Haunt Log.

targets.expr: _msg:"clock glitch burst" OR _msg:"name flicker hit" OR _msg:"whisper delivered" OR _msg:"invitation sent" OR _msg:"deadchannel joined" OR _msg:"runner created" OR _msg:"first contact bio screen" OR _msg:"haunt flag set" | filter username:* | filter username:~"$runner" | fields _time, _msg, username, hits, outcome, key, enabled | sort by (_time desc) | limit 50

panels.title: Haunt Log
panels.description: Every deadchannel line in one place, newest first: the gate, arming, each hit, the whisper, the invitation, the admin switches, and the runner's birth. The username is formatted into the message itself because the logs panel renders _msg and nothing else; expand a row for the counters and the trace id. The Runner variable filters it like the tables above.

targets.expr: _msg:"first contact" OR _msg:"haunt flag" OR _msg:"runner created" OR _msg:"deadchannel joined" | filter username:~"$runner" | format "[<username>] <_msg>" as _msg
